hints: Notice the question asks for a quantity, not a unit - so separate the names force and time from the names newton and second.
Recall the seven SI base quantities include mass, length, time, electric current, thermodynamic temperature, amount of substance and luminous intensity.
Check which of force and time can be expressed using other quantities, and which one is defined as fundamental.
walkthrough: Identify what each option names: force and time are physical quantities, while newton and second are units.
State the rule: an SI base quantity cannot be defined in terms of other quantities, and its unit is an SI base unit.
Test force: $F = ma$, so force has units $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$ and is built from mass, length and time, so it is derived.
Test second: it is the unit used to measure time, so it is an SI base unit but not a quantity.
Conclude that time is the fundamental quantity measured in seconds and belongs in the SI base set. This is option D.

options.A: Force is a quantity but it is a derived quantity with base units $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$, not an SI base quantity.
options.B: Newton is the SI derived unit of force, not the name of a quantity.
options.C: Second is the SI base unit for time, not the name of the base quantity itself.
options.D: Time is one of the seven SI base quantities and it is measured in seconds.
